While the introduction of MDR on UPI dominated India’s new-age tech discourse this week, startup funding fell sharply.

Fourteen startups raised $58.9 Mn, down 82% from the $321.9 Mn raised last week.

Key Startup Funding Highlights Of The Week

  • Enterprise services attracted the most capital this week, with three startups raising $42.5 Mn. Advertising services startup Flam accounted for the bulk of this funding with the week’s largest round of $40 Mn. 
  • Consumer services recorded three deals, with startups in the sector raising a total of $4.8 Mn. 
  • AJVC was the most active investor this week, backing MoroMaa, Beijan and Slayd. The VC firm also saw PE firm Novastar Partners as a limited partner for its fund. 
  • Five startups at the seed stage raised about $10.1 Mn, led by VerifAIX’s $5 Mn round.

Startup Fund Updates This Week

  • India Accelerator’s Finvolve announced the first close of its ₹250 Cr growth stage fund at ₹90 Cr. It intends to build a portfolio of 30-35 growth and late stage startups over the next three to four years.
  • AI focused VC firm Activate closed its maiden fund at $105 Mn within a year of its launch. It is targeting to back 25-30 startups operating across the AI sector. 
  • Dani Family Office’s Asiana Fund and Taiwan-based VC firm JC Capital launched the ₹1,000 Cr Asiana-JCC Advanced Manufacturing & Innovation Fund, with a primary corpus of ₹600 Cr and a green shoe option of ₹400 Cr.

Startup IPO Updates Of The Week

  • SEBI cleared the IPOs of Kuku Technologies and Fibe this week.
  • Rentomojo made a strong listing this week after receiving an overwhelming investor interest, giving hefty returns to early backers like Accel. 
  • After receiving SEBI approval for its IPO, Moneyview has now halved the fresh issue component to ₹750 Cr and trimmed the offer for sale (OFS) component to 10.04 Cr equity shares.
  • With greater clarity around the monetisation of UPI payments, PhonePe is set to revive its IPO plans. Inc42 learnt that the company would be looking to file its updated IPO papers for an IPO that could value it at about $10 Bn. The company is now targeting a listing between February-March 2027.

Other Developments Of The Week

  • Coursera-backed edtech startup Unstop acquired gaming startup PerspectAI for an undisclosed sum this week. The acquisition adds a combination of gaming and data science to Unstop’s engagement and hiring platform.
  • Over a month after Yulu’s $93 Mn Series C round, its early-backer 3one4 Capital announced that the round gave it a “successful, profitable” exit from the startup. The investor didn’t disclose who was the buyer of its stake in the secondary transaction.
  • Eyewear major Lenskart upped its stake in XR startup AjnaLens’ parent Dimension NXG with an ₹8 Cr investment to acquire an additional 1.8% stake in the startup.
  • PB Fintech’s board approved the acquisition of the remaining 20% stake in MyLoancare Ventures for ₹5 Cr to make it a wholly owned subsidiary. The board also approved capital infusions of up to ₹10 Cr into PB Wheels and ₹1 Cr into PB Financial Account Aggregator, both wholly owned subsidiaries.

Advanced hardware & technology and ecommerce sectors accounted for most of the week’s funding, raising a combined $201.1 Mn across eight deals. Together, they accounted for 62.5% of the total funding raised by Indian startups during the week.

Key Startup Funding Highlights Of The Week

  • Advanced hardware & technology emerged as the most-funded sector this week, with two startups raising a combined $121 Mn. The sector’s strong performance was largely driven by Pixxel’s mega $100 Mn round.
  • Following suit was ecommerce, which saw six startups raising $80 Mn. Nua’s $50 Mn fundraise was the biggest contributor, accounting for more than half of the sector’s total haul.
  • Beyond the top two sectors, AI also featured among the funded sectors. Meanwhile, foodtech clocked one deal and consumer services recorded two deals.
  • Early-stage funding remained subdued, with three startups raising a combined $3.3 Mn across pre-seed and seed rounds. This accounted for just 1% of the total $321.9 Mn raised during the week.
  • Peak XV Partners, Accel and Prath Ventures were the most active investors of the week, participating in two deals each.

Startup Fund Updates Of The Week

  • Healthtech-focused venture capital firm W Health Ventures closed its second fund at ₹700 Cr ($84 Mn), surpassing its initial ₹630 Cr target. The fund saw participation from family offices and institutional investors across India and the US.

Other Developments of The Week

  • EaseMyTrip cofounder and chairman Nishant Pitti has pledged 34.51 Cr shares, or 8.66% of the company’s total share capital, worth ₹211.9 Cr to Motilal Oswal Financial Services for “personal use”.
  • Circle Internet Group has agreed to acquire Peak XV-backed B2B cross-border payments startup Tazapay in an all-stock deal reportedly valued at nearly $400 Mn.
  • Swiggy is set to sell B2B retail distribution platform LYNK to Udaan in a share-swap deal, valuing the startup at ₹500 Cr. In return, the foodtech major will pick up a 2.8% stake in the B2B ecommerce unicorn. Swiggy will also invest another ₹75 Cr in Udaan for an additional 0.4% stake.

India’s startup funding market opened September on a softer note, extending its decline for a second straight week. Between August 31 and September 4, 22 startups raised a combined $176.5 Mn, down 16% from the $210.3 Mn raised across 23 deals in the previous week.

Healthtech and cleantech accounted for most of the week’s funding, raising a combined $120.8 Mn across nine deals. Together, they captured nearly 68% of the total raised by Indian startups during the week.

Key Startup Funding Highlights Of The Week

  • Healthtech was the most funded sector this week, with four startups raising a combined $74.5 Mn. The strong week for the sector was largely a one-startup story. Ultrahuman’s $70 Mn round made up 94% of the sector’s total funding.
  • Cleantech trailed healthtech with five startups raising $46.3 Mn this week. Yuma Energy’s $35 Mn fundraise provided the biggest boost, accounting for a substantial chunk of the sector’s haul.
  • Beyond the top two sectors, advanced hardware and technology and ecommerce segments saw four funding deals materialise apiece.
  • Early-stage funding remained active, with six startups collectively raising around $12 Mn across seed, pre-seed and pre-Series A rounds. The week also saw three startups raise undisclosed amounts in equity.
  • On the investor front, Equentis and Info Edge Ventures were the week’s most active backers, participating in two startup deals each.

  • upGrad completed the acquisition of Unacademy for just over $200 Mn, marking a more than 90% drop from its $3.5 Bn peak valuation in 2021.
  • Adobe acquired Peak XV Partners’ backed startup Rilo, backed by Peak XV Partners, for an undisclosed amount. It is Adobe’s second Indian startup acquisition after Rephrase.ai in 2023.
  • Niyo agreed to acquire Capital India Finance’s RemitX business for ₹11.4 Cr, expanding its forex and cross-border payments play.
  • Truemeds is said to be eyeing the buy out of ecommerce unicorn DealShare via a share-swap deal that could value it at over $90 Mn, far below its $1.7 Bn peak valuation.

Startup IPO Developments This Week

  • After an overwhelming investor response to its IPO, AI cloud provider ESDS Software Solution made a strong public market debut, listing at an over 75% premium on the bourses. The stock closed at ₹908.4, gaining 111.7% on its first trading day.
  • After ESDS, Yotta Data Services is also planning to go public. The company is likely to file its draft papers with SEBI by October, eyeing the raise of up to $1.5 Bn via its IPO.
  • Pernia’s Pop-Up Shop’s parent Purple Labs ₹680 Cr IPO was oversubscribed by 1.29X on the final day, with retail investors leading demand at 1.57X. The shares are set to list on Monday (September 7).

Other Developments Of The Week

  • Fintech unicorn-turned-SFB slice is reportedly raising around $100 Mn at a $450 Mn-$465 Mn valuation, down sharply from its previous $1.25 Bn valuation. The round could see participation from Neo Group, Kado Global and Moore Strategic Ventures.
  • Jagdish Farshan has raised ₹43.5 Cr ($4.6 Mn) in its first institutional round, led by Sharrp Ventures and angel investors, as the 88-year-old brand looks to expand through quick commerce.

Key Startup Funding Highlights Of The Week

  • Fintech segment regained the top funded startup segment title this week on the back of KreditBee’s $280 Mn funding round. Besides, GoSats also netted $5 Mn this week. 
  • In terms of deal count, AI and ecommerce sectors recorded the highest six deals each this week. While AI startups raised $30.3 Mn, ecommerce startups netted $25.8 Mn, respectively.
  • Seed funding skyrocketed 940% to $22.9 Mn in the week under review, from $2.2 Mn in the previous week
  • IAN Group and Unicorn India Ventures’ were the most active startup investors this week, backing two startups each. 

Startup IPO Updates This Week

  • Study abroad startup Leverage Edu has initiated discussions with investment bankers for an ₹2,000-3,000 Cr IPO in the upcoming 12-18 months.
  • CureFit onboarded four independent directors — JPMorgan’s Kalpana Morparia, Celesta Capital’s Arun Kumar, Ayushman Bharat’s Indu Bhushan, OpenAI’s Pragya Misra — on its board ahead of its IPO. 

Other Developments Of The Week

  • Exotel acquihired the leadership team of voice AI platform Dubverse, including cofounders Anuja Dhawan and Varshul Gupta to strengthen its AI capabilities for enterprise CX 
  • Investment firm Bay Capital Partners appointed Sandeep Barasia (former Delhivery CBO) and Tej Kapoor (former IvyCap Ventures MD) as partners to helm its upcoming digital fund
  • PE firm TR Capital committed to invest $1 Bn in India via secondaries over the next five years. It has also appointed Umang Agarwal as its India MD, along with multiple senior leaders.
